title: Singing basics
examples: What is the best way to breathe when I sing?
Should I stand straight when I sing a song?
What kind of exercises help my voice before singing?

explain.say: First we talk about good breathing for singing.
Next we look at good posture for singing.
Then we learn about singing warm-ups.
Our next topic is understanding pitch in singing.
For a real-life example, think about a playground song.
A common mistake is holding your breath when singing.

faq.q: Why is breathing so important for singing?
faq.a: Good breath support gives you the power to sing notes for a long time. You can also use your diaphragm to control the air flow.
asks: How do I breathe for singing?
Is breath control important for singers?

faq.q: What should I do before I sing a big song?
faq.a: You should always do warm-ups first. This gently prepares your vocal cords so they do not get hurt.
asks: Do I need to warm up my voice?
What is the best warm-up exercise?

faq.q: Does my posture really affect how well I sing?
faq.a: Yes, standing tall helps your breath move freely. Good posture allows your voice to project without strain.
asks: Should I slouch when I sing?
How does my body affect my singing?

faq.q: What is the difference between high and low pitch?
faq.a: Pitch is how high or low a sound sounds. Low notes vibrate slower, and high notes vibrate faster.
asks: How do I sing a high note?

faq.q: Can I just start singing without warming up?
faq.a: It is better not to. Starting cold can strain your voice. Gentle warm-ups are always the safest way to begin.
asks: Is it okay to skip warm-ups?
What if I feel tired before singing?

facts: Breathing for singing uses the diaphragm muscle.
Good posture keeps the airway open and relaxed.
Warm-ups gradually increase vocal cord tension.
Pitch refers to the frequency of a sound wave.

quiz.say: To sing a long, sustained note, which body part should you focus on using?
quiz.why: The diaphragm is the main muscle that controls your breath support for singing.

wrong.0: Focusing only on your chest can lead to shallow, quick breaths.
wrong.1: Using your throat muscles strains the voice and limits your breath.
wrong.2: Shoulders should be relaxed; tension there blocks airflow.

quiz.say: If you are singing a very high note, what should your posture help you maintain?
quiz.why: A straight spine aligns your body, allowing the sound to travel freely from your breath.

wrong.0: Slouching compresses your lungs and limits your air supply.
wrong.1: Tension in the neck pulls the head and restricts breath flow.
wrong.3: Leaning forward restricts your diaphragm's ability to expand fully.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of doing lip trills before singing?

options.show: To warm up the lips and jaw muscles
options.say: To warm up the lips and jaw muscles

options.show: To make your voice sound louder
options.say: To make your voice sound louder

options.show: To improve your singing range only
options.say: To improve your singing range only

quiz.why: Lip trills gently vibrate your lips, which helps warm up the facial muscles used in singing.

wrong.1: Lip trills are for warming up, not for jumping between pitches.
wrong.2: Loudness comes from breath support, not the trill itself.
wrong.3: They warm up the whole area, not just the highest notes.
